title: IPv4 Addressing
summary: IPv4 addressing identifies hosts and networks using 32-bit addresses.

concepts.name: IPv4 address
concepts.description: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit logical address written in dotted decimal form.

concepts.name: Subnet mask
concepts.description: A subnet mask separates the network part from the host part of an IPv4 address.

notes.overview: IPv4 addresses help devices identify source and destination hosts across IP networks.
notes.core_concept: An IPv4 address has a network portion and a host portion.
notes.explanation: The subnet mask tells which bits describe the network and which bits identify the host.
notes.example: In 192.168.1.10/24, 192.168.1.0 is the network and .10 identifies a host in that network.

common_mistake.content: A common mistake is treating the subnet mask as the device address; it only describes the network boundary.
common_mistake.misconception: confuses subnet mask with host address

quick_check.content: Check the role of the subnet mask.
quick_check.question: What does /24 tell you in an IPv4 address?
quick_check.answer: The first 24 bits are the network portion.

notes.simple_explanation: An IPv4 address is like a house address, and the subnet tells which neighborhood it belongs to.
notes.analogy: The network part is the street name, while the host part is the house number.
notes.advanced_example: CIDR notation lets networks use flexible prefix lengths like /26 or /30.
notes.edge_case: The first and last addresses in many IPv4 subnets are reserved for network and broadcast use.
notes.challenge_question: How many usable host addresses are available in a /30 IPv4 subnet?
